content: 1. Administer trimethoprim at a dose of 100 mg orally every 12 hours. It can also be used in combination with sulfamethoxazole (e.g., Cotrim, Bactrim, Septra, Sulfatrim) for urinary tract infections caused by Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Proteus mirabilis, or coagulase-negative Staphylococcus species. 2. The safety and efficacy of trimethoprim in children under 12 years of age have not been established. 3. Both amiodarone and trimethoprim can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 4. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 5. Apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, can reduce the exposure of drugs metabolized by CYP3A4. Avoid or substitute other drugs when possible. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for loss of therapeutic effect and adjust the dose as per prescribing information. 6. Trimethoprim reduces the efficacy of live BCG vaccines due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 7. Trimethoprim reduces the efficacy of the cholera vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received systemic antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 8. Both disopyramide and trimethoprim can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 9. Trimethoprim increases the levels or effects of erdafitinib by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP2C9 inhibitors is unavoidable, closely monitor for adverse reactions and adjust the erdafitinib dose accordingly. 10. Trimethoprim increases the levels or effects of etrasimod. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Increased exposure to etrasimod is expected in patients who are CYP2C9 poor metabolizers when coadministered with moderate to strong CYP2C8 inhibitors. 11. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, and coadministration may increase the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. 12. Both ibutilide and trimethoprim can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 13. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor; avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. 14. Both indapamide and trimethoprim can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 15. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates with ivosidenib or replace them with alternative therapies. 16. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of sensitive CYP2C9 substrates with ivosidenib or replace them with alternative therapies. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for loss of therapeutic effect. 17. Leucovorin reduces the efficacy of trimethoprim due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor for treatment failure or reduced efficacy of trimethoprim, especially when used with sulfamethoxazole for Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia in HIV-positive patients. 18. Levoleucovorin reduces the efficacy of trimethoprim due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor for treatment failure or reduced efficacy of trimethoprim, especially when used with sulfamethoxazole for Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia in HIV-positive patients. 19. Lonafarnib increases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. 20. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of trimethoprim by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Mefloquine may enhance the QTc-prolonging effect of high-risk QTc-prolonging agents. 22. Trimethoprim and methotrexate both increase each other's toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Trimethoprim has been shown to rarely increase bone marrow suppression in patients receiving methotrexate due to an additive antifolate effect. 23. Trimethoprim reduces the efficacy of oral microbiota by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Oral microbiota contains bacterial spores, and antibacterial agents may decrease its efficacy. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating oral microbiota. 24. Both pentamidine and trimethoprim can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 25. Both pimozide and trimethoprim can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 26. Both procainamide and trimethoprim can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 27. Both quinidine and trimethoprim can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 28. Trimethoprim increases the levels or effects of siponimod by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Coadministration of siponimod with drugs causing moderate CYP2C9 and moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibition is not recommended. Exercise caution if siponimod is coadministered with moderate CYP2C9 inhibitors alone. 29. Both sotalol and trimethoprim can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 30. Tafenoquine increases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by inhibiting organic cation transporter-2 (OCT2) and multidrug and toxin extrusion (MATE) transporters in vitro. Avoid coadministration with OCT2 or MATE substrates. If coadministration cannot be avoided, monitor for substrate-related toxicities and consider dosage reduction based on product labeling. 31. Trimethoprim increases the levels or effects of tovorafenib by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of tovorafenib (a CYP2C8 substrate) with strong or moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors. 32. Trilaciclib decreases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by inhibiting OCT2, MATE1, and MATE-2K transporters. Avoid coadministration with substrates where minimal increased concentration in the kidney or blood may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. 33. Trimethoprim increases the levels or effects of tucatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use of tucatinib with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose according to product labeling. 34. Trimethoprim reduces the efficacy of live typhoid vaccines due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 35. Both trimethoprim and aliskiren increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. Trimethoprim decreases urinary potassium excretion and may cause hyperkalemia, particularly with high doses, renal insufficiency, or when combined with other drugs that cause hyperkalemia. 36. Alpelisib decreases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 37. Trimethoprim increases the levels of amantadine by decreasing its elimination. Use caution and monitor. Coadministration may impair renal clearance of amantadine, resulting in higher plasma concentrations. 38. Both trimethoprim and amiloride increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. Trimethoprim decreases urinary potassium excretion and may cause hyperkalemia, particularly with high doses, renal insufficiency, or when combined with other drugs that cause hyperkalemia. 39. Amiodarone increases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor. 40. Both amitriptyline and trimethoprim can prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 41. Both amoxapine and trimethoprim can prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 42. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Coadministration of apalutamide, a weak CYP2C9 inducer, with CYP2C9 substrates can result in lower exposure to these medications. Evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect if coadministration is necessary. 43. Both artemether/lumefantrine and trimethoprim can prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 44. Trimethoprim decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 45. Both trimethoprim and benazepril increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. Trimethoprim decreases urinary potassium excretion and may cause hyperkalemia, particularly with high doses, renal insufficiency, or when combined with other drugs that cause hyperkalemia. 46. Both trimethoprim and canagliflozin increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. 47. Both trimethoprim and candesartan increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. Trimethoprim decreases urinary potassium excretion and may cause hyperkalemia, particularly with high doses, renal insufficiency, or when combined with other drugs that cause hyperkalemia. 48. Cannabidiol increases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by inhibiting CYP2C9 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Cannabidiol may potentially inhibit CYP2C9 activity. Consider reducing the dose when concomitantly using CYP2C9 substrates. 49. Both trimethoprim and captopril increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. Trimethoprim decreases urinary potassium excretion and may cause hyperkalemia, particularly with high doses, renal insufficiency, or when combined with other drugs that cause hyperkalemia. 50. Both chlorpromazine and trimethoprim can prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 51. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor. 52. Both clarithromycin and trimethoprim can prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 53. Both clomipramine and trimethoprim can prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 54. Trimethoprim decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 55. Crofelemer increases the levels of trimethoprim by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Crofelemer has the potential to inhibit CYP3A4 at concentrations expected in the gut but is unlikely to inhibit systemically due to minimal absorption. 56. Both trimethoprim and cyclosporine increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. Trimethoprim decreases urinary potassium excretion and may cause hyperkalemia, particularly with high doses, renal insufficiency, or when combined with other drugs that cause hyperkalemia. 57. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 58. Trimethoprim increases the levels or effects of daprodustat. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors increase daprodustat exposure. If coadministered with moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors, reduce the daprodustat starting dose by half (except if the starting dose is already 1 mg). Monitor hemoglobin and adjust the daprodustat dose when initiating or stopping therapy with moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors during treatment. 59. Trimethoprim increases the toxicity of topical dapsone by decreasing its metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Coadministration increases systemic exposure to dapsone and its metabolites (N-acetyl-dapsone, dapsone hydroxylamine). This may induce methemoglobinemia. 60. Both desipramine and trimethoprim can prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 61. Trimethoprim increases the levels or effects of digoxin by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. Digoxin increases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor. 62. Dofetilide increases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by competing for renal tubular clearance. Both dofetilide and trimethoprim can prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 63. Both dolasetron and trimethoprim can prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 64. Both doxepin and trimethoprim can prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 65. Both dronedarone and trimethoprim can prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 66. Both droperidol and trimethoprim can prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 67. Elagolix decreases the levels of trimethoprim by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates if coadministered. Consider increasing the CYP3A substrate dose if needed. 68. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases the levels of trimethoprim by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Elvitegravir decreases the levels of trimethoprim by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Elvitegravir is a moderate CYP2C9 inducer. 69. Both trimethoprim and enalapril increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. Trimethoprim decreases urinary potassium excretion and may cause hyperkalemia, particularly with high doses, renal insufficiency, or when combined with other drugs that cause hyperkalemia. 70. Encorafenib affects trimethoprim metabolism by inhibiting and inducing CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Use caution and monitor. Coadministration of encorafenib with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may result in increased toxicity or decreased efficacy of these agents.
